newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight activity quiet, Iran demand returns.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight activity quiet, Iran demand returns.

text.p: Activity on London's sugar freight market was subdued on Tuesday with the most significant feature being the re-emergence of Iran as a destination, shipbrokers said.
E D & F Man quoted for 14,000 tonnes min/max bagged sugar from Durban to Iran for mid-August, they said.
Little physical demand has been seen in recent weeks from Iran, which has bought increased steady amounts of both white and raw sugar throughout the year.
In other new business, CSR quoted for 20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Ho Chi Minh City for prompt dates.
According to the Baltic Exchange list, the rate achieved by CSR on its recent 20,000 tonnes min/max fixture from Queensland to Surabaya was $17.00.
Mauritius Sugar Syndicate was thought to have fixed 18,800/19,200 tonnes of bulk sugar from Port Louis to US Gulf/Atlantic August 4/9.

Czarnikow Rionda fixed 21,500/24,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Rosario to US Gulf/Atlantic for early August and Cargill fixed 25,000 tonnes from Santos or Paranagua to Baltic/Med/Black Sea for early August at under $30.
